bank.name: Muslim Rule in South Asia
bank.subject: Islamic Studies
bank.description: Muslim dynasties, rulers and their legacy in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.prompt: Muhammad bin Qasim invaded Sindh during the reign of which caliph?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim was sent by Hajjaj bin Yusuf during the reign of Umayyad caliph Al-Walid I.

questions.prompt: Who defeated Raja Dahir, the ruler of Sindh?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir in 712 CE.

questions.prompt: Which ruler invaded India seventeen times and plundered the Somnath temple?
questions.explanation: Mahmud of Ghazni (971-1030) made 17 raids into India, including the famous Somnath raid of 1025.

questions.prompt: Who founded the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: Qutubuddin Aibak, a slave-general of Ghori, founded the Slave dynasty in 1206.

questions.prompt: The Qutub Minar in Delhi was started by which ruler?
questions.explanation: Qutubuddin Aibak began the Qutub Minar; Iltutmish completed it.

questions.prompt: Which Delhi Sultanate ruler introduced the silver coin 'Tanka' and gold 'Jital'?
questions.explanation: Shams-ud-din Iltutmish introduced the Tanka (silver) and Jital (copper) currency.

questions.prompt: Which Sultan of Delhi is famous for his 'blood and iron' policy and breaking the power of the 'Forty'?
questions.explanation: Balban (1266-1287) ruled with an iron hand and crushed the noble council known as the Chahalgani.

questions.prompt: Which ruler repelled the Mongol invasions of India in the 13th century?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji (1296-1316) successfully repelled repeated Mongol invasions.

questions.prompt: Who built the Alai Darwaza and tried to introduce market price controls?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji introduced market reforms and built the Alai Darwaza in Delhi.

questions.prompt: Which Tughlaq sultan shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-1351) famously moved the capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri).

questions.prompt: Which ruler is remembered for constructing canals, gardens and cities during the Tughlaq period?
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq (1351-1388) built canals, gardens, hospitals and the city of Hissar.

questions.prompt: Who invaded India in 1398 and sacked Delhi, weakening the Tughlaq dynasty?
questions.explanation: Amir Taimur's invasion of 1398 devastated Delhi and left the Sultanate in decline.

questions.prompt: Who established the Lodi dynasty, the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: Bahlol Lodi founded the Lodi dynasty in 1451.

questions.prompt: Who was the last ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, defeated at Panipat in 1526?
questions.explanation: Ibrahim Lodi was defeated and killed by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

questions.prompt: Who defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526?
questions.explanation: Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire, defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526.

questions.prompt: Who defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar at the Battle of Khanwa in 1527?
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Rana Sanga at Khanwa in 1527, consolidating Mughal rule in North India.

questions.prompt: Who defeated Humayun and ruled Delhi for five years (1540-1545) as an Afghan ruler?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri drove Humayun out of India and ruled from 1540 to 1545.

questions.prompt: Sher Shah Suri is credited with introducing which famous road?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri built the Grand Trunk Road from Bengal to the northwest, still in use today.

questions.prompt: The 'Din-i-Ilahi' was introduced by which emperor?
questions.explanation: Akbar introduced Din-i-Ilahi in 1582, a syncretic religious movement.

questions.prompt: Which Mughal emperor issued the 'Farman' of 1857-style religious edicts and is buried in Aurangabad?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb (1658-1707), the last great Mughal, is buried in Khuldabad, near Aurangabad.

questions.prompt: The Mughal Empire reached its greatest territorial extent under which emperor?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb expanded the empire to its largest extent, covering almost all of the subcontinent.

questions.prompt: The 'Badshahi Mosque' in Lahore was built by which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb built the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore in 1673.

questions.prompt: Which ruler is famous for the 'Farman' promoting Urdu and building the Aligarh traditions later?
options: No Mughal did; Sir Syed later promoted Urdu education
questions.explanation: Urdu flourished under the later Mughals and was promoted by Sir Syed's Aligarh movement.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Muslim woman ruler of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Razia Sultana (1236-1240) was the only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.prompt: Which Mughal empress wielded great power during Jahangir's reign?
questions.explanation: Nur Jahan, Jahangir's wife, effectively co-ruled the empire.

questions.prompt: Who defeated the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761?
questions.explanation: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas at Panipat in 1761.

questions.prompt: The 'Sultanate of Bengal' and 'Deccan sultanates' were examples of?
options: Regional Muslim kingdoms of South Asia
questions.explanation: Bengal and the Deccan sultanates were independent Muslim kingdoms before Mughal expansion.

questions.prompt: Who founded the city of Hyderabad (Deccan)?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad in 1591.

questions.prompt: The 'Charminar' monument is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Charminar, built in 1591, is Hyderabad's iconic monument.

questions.prompt: Which ruler built the 'Shalimar Gardens' in Kashmir and Lahore?
questions.explanation: Jahangir laid the Kashmir Shalimar; Shah Jahan built Lahore's Shalimar.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim ruler of Kashmir is famed for building the 'Mughal Gardens'?
options: The Mughals built them; Jahangir was enamored of Kashmir
questions.explanation: Jahangir and Shah Jahan built Kashmir's terraced Mughal gardens.

questions.prompt: The 'Jizya' tax policy of Aurangzeb was notable because?
options: It was reimposed on non-Muslims, unlike Akbar's abolition
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb reimposed Jizya, reversing Akbar's policy of abolishing it.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim ruler's tomb, the 'Taj Mahal', took 22 years to build?
options: Shah Jahan built it for Mumtaz Mahal
Jahangir built it for Nur Jahan
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal (1632-1653) as Mumtaz Mahal's mausoleum.

questions.prompt: Who established the Slave Dynasty in Delhi?
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-Din Aibak founded the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty.

questions.prompt: The Qutb Minar in Delhi was started by:
questions.explanation: Aibak began the Qutb Minar; successors completed it.

questions.prompt: Which ruler of the Delhi Sultanate introduced the 'Dagh' (branding of horses) system?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji reformed the military with the Dagh.

questions.prompt: The Tughlaq ruler famous for his ambitious but failed projects was:
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq is known for his grand experiments.

questions.prompt: The Delhi Sultanate was defeated at Panipat by Babur in:
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat in 1526.

questions.prompt: The first Mughal emperor was:
questions.explanation: Babur founded the Mughal Empire in 1526.

questions.prompt: Who was the Mughal emperor that restored the empire after Sher Shah's interregnum?
questions.explanation: Humayun reclaimed the throne in 1555.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar and:
questions.explanation: Akbar defeated Hemu at the Second Battle of Panipat.

questions.prompt: Sher Shah Suri is remembered for:
options: The Grand Trunk Road and land reforms
questions.explanation: Sher Shah built the GT Road and reformed administration.

questions.prompt: The rupee currency system was refined by:
questions.explanation: Sher Shah issued the standard silver rupiya.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Plassey (1757) marked the beginning of:
questions.explanation: Plassey paved the way for British dominance.

questions.prompt: The Fatahpur Sikri was built by:
questions.explanation: Akbar founded Fatehpur Sikri in 1571.

questions.prompt: The Maratha Empire rose after the decline of which power?
questions.explanation: Marathas filled the vacuum left by Mughal decline.

questions.prompt: The first Anglo-Sikh War ended with the Treaty of:
questions.explanation: The 1846 Treaty of Lahore ended the first war.

questions.prompt: The Mughal emperor who banned music at court in later life was:
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb discouraged music in his later years.

questions.prompt: The 'Jharokha Darshan' tradition was started by:
questions.explanation: Akbar introduced public appearances at the jharokha.

questions.prompt: Muhammad bin Qasim was approximately how old when he conquered Sindh?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim led the conquest of Sindh at about the age of seventeen.

questions.prompt: The Arab conquest of Sindh took place in which year?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711 CE.

questions.prompt: Hajjaj bin Yusuf, who dispatched Muhammad bin Qasim, was the governor of?
questions.explanation: Hajjaj bin Yusuf was the powerful Umayyad governor of Iraq.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct chronological order of the Delhi Sultanate dynasties?
questions.explanation: The five dynasties ran: Mamluk (Slave), Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi.

questions.prompt: Who founded the Khalji dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: Jalal-ud-din Khalji founded the Khalji dynasty in 1290.

questions.prompt: Alauddin Khalji was the nephew and son-in-law of whom?
questions.explanation: Alauddin rose against his uncle Jalal-ud-din Khalji and took the throne.

questions.prompt: Alauddin Khalji's general Malik Kafur campaigned in which region?
questions.explanation: Malik Kafur led the Deccan campaigns, conquering Devagiri and other states.

questions.prompt: Who founded the Sayyid dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: Khizr Khan, formerly a Tughlaq governor, founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414.

questions.prompt: Who was the last ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty?
questions.explanation: Nasir-ud-din Mahmud was the last Tughlaq ruler, who lost Delhi to Khizr Khan.

questions.prompt: Razia Sultana was the daughter of which sultan?
questions.explanation: Razia Sultana, the first woman ruler of Delhi, was Iltutmish's daughter.

questions.prompt: Iltutmish was the slave and successor of whom?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish, a trusted slave of Aibak, succeeded him as Sultan of Delhi.

questions.prompt: Iltutmish shifted the capital of the Delhi Sultanate from Lahore to where?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish moved the capital to Delhi, making it the seat of the sultanate.

questions.prompt: Iltutmish obtained a robe of honour from the Abbasid caliph of which city?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish received recognition from the Abbasid caliph in Baghdad.

questions.prompt: Who were the 'Chahalgani' (the Forty)?
options: A group of Turkish nobles of the Slave dynasty
questions.explanation: The Forty were the powerful Turkish slave nobles who dominated the early sultanate.

questions.prompt: Mahmud of Ghazni was the son of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Mahmud was the son of Sabuktigin, the Ghaznavid ruler.

questions.prompt: Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan at which battle?
questions.explanation: In 1192, Ghori avenged his earlier defeat and crushed Prithviraj at the Second Tarain.

questions.prompt: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori at which battle?
questions.explanation: At the First Tarain (1191) Prithviraj defeated Ghori, who returned to conquer in 1192.

questions.prompt: Qutubuddin Aibak was the general of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Aibak served as a general of Muhammad Ghori and later founded the Slave dynasty.

questions.prompt: The Mamluk dynasty of Delhi is also known as?
questions.explanation: The Mamluk or Slave dynasty was founded by Qutubuddin Aibak.

questions.prompt: Who completed the construction of the Qutub Minar?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish completed the Qutub Minar begun by Aibak.

questions.prompt: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced which disastrous economic experiment?
options: Token currency of brass and copper
questions.explanation: His token coinage, without proper control, was forged widely and failed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following cities was founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
questions.explanation: Firoz Shah founded cities such as Hissar, Firozabad and Jaunpur.

questions.prompt: Which Lodi ruler founded the city of Agra?
questions.explanation: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and shifted his capital there.

questions.prompt: Before invading India, Babur ruled which region?
questions.explanation: Babur was the ruler of Ferghana and Kabul before conquering Delhi.

questions.prompt: Which autobiography did Babur write?
questions.explanation: Babur's memoirs, the Baburnama, are a celebrated account of his life.

questions.prompt: Humayun's tomb in Delhi was built by whom?
questions.explanation: Humayun's widow, Haji Begum, built the garden tomb completed in the 1570s.

questions.prompt: Who served as Akbar's regent in the early years of his reign?
questions.explanation: Bairam Khan guided young Akbar until the emperor assumed full power.

questions.prompt: In which year did Akbar abolish the Jizya tax?
questions.explanation: Akbar abolished the Jizya in 1564.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was one of Akbar's 'Navratnas' (nine gems)?
questions.explanation: The musician Tansen was among Akbar's nine court gems.

questions.prompt: Tansen was the celebrated court musician of which emperor?
questions.explanation: Tansen graced the court of Akbar.

questions.prompt: Akbar built the Ibadat Khana (House of Worship) at which place?
questions.explanation: The Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri hosted interfaith religious debates.

questions.prompt: The Peacock Throne was built by which emperor?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan commissioned the jewel-encrusted Peacock Throne.

questions.prompt: The Peacock Throne was later carried away to Persia by whom?
questions.explanation: Nadir Shah looted the Peacock Throne after sacking Delhi in 1739.

questions.prompt: Aurangzeb ruled for approximately how many years?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb reigned from 1658 to 1707 — about 49 years.

questions.prompt: In the war of succession, Aurangzeb defeated which brother?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb defeated Dara Shukoh, Shuja and Murad to take the throne.

questions.prompt: Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to which city after 1857?
questions.explanation: The British exiled Zafar to Rangoon, where he died in 1862.

questions.prompt: Tipu Sultan ruled which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan ruled the kingdom of Mysore.

questions.prompt: Tipu Sultan is popularly known as?
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan earned the title 'Tiger of Mysore'.

questions.prompt: What was the capital of Tipu Sultan's kingdom?
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan ruled from Srirangapatna.

questions.prompt: Tipu Sultan died fighting in which war?
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan was killed defending Srirangapatna in 1799.

questions.prompt: The English East India Company established its first factory in India at?
questions.explanation: The Company set up its first factory at Surat in 1612.

questions.prompt: Siraj-ud-Daulah was the Nawab of which region?
questions.explanation: Siraj-ud-Daulah was the Nawab of Bengal before Plassey.

questions.prompt: Who betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah at the Battle of Plassey?
questions.explanation: Mir Jafar's defection handed the British victory at Plassey in 1757.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought by the British against whom?
questions.explanation: At Buxar, the British defeated Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II.

questions.prompt: Who founded the Mysore dynasty?
questions.explanation: Hyder Ali rose to power and founded the effective Mysore dynasty.

questions.prompt: The Nizams of Hyderabad belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Asaf Jahi dynasty ruled Hyderabad from 1724.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Nizam of Hyderabad?
questions.explanation: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah founded the Hyderabad state.

questions.prompt: The Qutb Shahi dynasty ruled which region?
questions.explanation: The Qutb Shahis ruled Golconda and founded Hyderabad city.

questions.prompt: Which Ghurid ruler laid the foundation of lasting Muslim rule in North India?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ghori's victories set up the Delhi Sultanate under his general Aibak.

questions.prompt: The First Battle of Panipat led to the establishment of which empire?
questions.explanation: Babur's victory at Panipat (1526) founded Mughal rule in India.

questions.prompt: Sher Shah Suri's tomb is located at?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah's red sandstone mausoleum stands at Sasaram, Bihar.
